key_patterns.name: Multiplex social layers with differing tie strengths
key_patterns.description: Family, work/school, and community layers have distinct contact frequencies and influence strengths; family ties are denser and stronger, community ties sparser and weaker.
key_patterns.relevance: Justifies layer-specific influence weights and contact scheduling; affects adoption speed and cascade reach.

key_patterns.name: Demographic and occupational homophily
key_patterns.description: Agents are more connected to others sharing age_group and/or occupation, especially in family and work/school layers.
key_patterns.relevance: Homophily concentrates influence within groups, creating within-group cascades and between-group adoption lags.

key_patterns.name: Heterogeneous degree distributions
key_patterns.description: Family degree is low and narrow; work/school has moderate degree; community has right-skewed degree with hubs.
key_patterns.relevance: Degree heterogeneity drives early adoption among highly connected agents and impacts cascade size distribution and time to 50% adoption.

key_patterns.name: Risk perception heterogeneity
key_patterns.description: risk_perception spans [0,1] and is expected to be skewed (often Beta-like). Higher risk_perception lowers the social threshold for adoption.
key_patterns.relevance: Supports mapping risk_perception to adoption thresholds/utility and calibrating group-specific baselines.

key_patterns.name: Behavioral persistence and churn
key_patterns.description: Agents tend to persist in current behavior with occasional switching, influenced by information exposure and neighbor norms.
key_patterns.relevance: Required to model norm_churn_rate and to avoid unrealistically fast oscillations.

key_patterns.name: Neighbor-norm sensitivity
key_patterns.description: Adoption likelihood increases with the fraction of neighbors wearing masks, with strongest effect from family and work/school.
key_patterns.relevance: Core mechanism for social contagion; informs peer influence coefficients and layer weights.

key_distributions.name: Degree by layer
key_distributions.description: Distribution of node degrees per layer (family, work/school, community) and aggregated degree.
key_distributions.parameters: mean_k_layer, sd_k_layer, Q10/Q50/Q90, tail_index for community if heavy-tailed

key_distributions.name: Layer overlap
key_distributions.description: Distribution of edge multiplexity (same dyad present on multiple layers).
key_distributions.parameters: P(overlap=2), P(overlap=3) per dyad; mean overlap per node

key_distributions.name: Risk perception
key_distributions.parameters: Beta(a,b) fitted via method-of-moments or MLE; group-specific means by age_group×occupation

key_distributions.name: Initial adoption (day 0)
key_distributions.description: Share of agents wearing masks at day 0 overall and by group.

key_distributions.name: Exposure frequency
key_distributions.description: Distribution of received_info per agent per day.

key_distributions.name: Clustering and component sizes
key_distributions.description: Local clustering coefficients and connected component sizes per layer.

num_agents.notes: Count unique IDs across keys and all adjacency lists.

edge_direction.notes: Symmetrize adjacency lists to ensure undirected ties; remove self-loops and duplicates.

layer_weights.notes: Multiply neighbor_mask_share by these weights before aggregation; calibrate via likelihood fit.

degree_distributions.notes: Compute degree histograms and quantiles for adoption_by_degree_quantile metric.

homophily_mixing_matrices.notes: Used to generate synthetic edges for counterfactuals and to weight influence within/between groups.

layer_overlap_multiplier.notes: If a neighbor appears on multiple layers, multiply their influence by this factor; calibrate if needed.

baseline_adoption_by_group.notes: Use day 0 wearing_mask to set initial probabilities per group; shrink with hierarchical prior.

risk_threshold_mapping.notes: Adopt if weighted_neighbor_signal >= max(min_threshold, threshold_base - risk_slope*risk_perception).

persistence_inertia.notes: Controls norm_churn_rate; refine via MLE on transition counts.

stubborn_fraction.notes: Share of agents with fixed state regardless of social influence; helps match tails of churn and cascades.

adoption_logit_coefficients.source: mask-wearing diffusion simulation CSV (panel) + social_network.json (neighbor shares) + agent_attributes.csv
adoption_logit_coefficients.notes: Starting values; calibrate via logistic or cloglog discrete-time hazard model. neighbor_share is layer-weighted.

nonlinear_reinforcement.source: fit to curvature of adoption vs neighbor_share
nonlinear_reinforcement.notes: Exponent >1 increases conformity effects; tune to match cascade_size_distribution.

within_group_influence_multiplier.notes: Multiply influence from neighbors sharing age_group or occupation.

exposure_model.value: Bernoulli per layer per day with probability proportional to degree and layer weight
exposure_model.notes: Use received_info to fit per-layer exposure rates.

baseline_exogenous_info_rate.notes: Daily probability of receiving info from non-network sources; calibrate to match observed exposure frequency.

info_effect_on_adoption.notes: Multiplier on adoption odds when received_info==True.

mandate_start_day.source: mask-wearing diffusion simulation CSV (structural break detection) or scenario design
mandate_start_day.notes: If a known policy date exists, fix; else cross-validate over candidate days to maximize policy_attribution_fraction fit.

policy_targeting.notes: Apply stronger enforcement in work/school contexts.

policy_compliance_probability.source: fit to step-changes in adoption in targeted groups
policy_compliance_probability.notes: Direct probability to adopt under active mandate absent social signal.

enforcement_spillover_to_peers.source: estimate from changes in non-targeted neighbors
enforcement_spillover_to_peers.notes: Fraction of policy-induced adoption that diffuses to peers as social signal.

seed_selection_rule.value: probability proportional to risk_perception and degree
seed_selection_rule.notes: If day 0 data unavailable, seed initial adopters based on intrinsic risk and connectivity.

initial_mask_state.value: from day 0 wearing_mask if available; else draw Bernoulli with p0_by_group
initial_mask_state.notes: Ensures alignment with observed starting conditions.

metrics_alignment.notes: Compute at each run for calibration/validation.

preprocessing_steps.purpose: Cast social_network.json keys to int, ensure agent_id alignment across files.
Add reciprocal edges, drop self-loops/duplicates; compute degrees, clustering, components by layer.
Merge agent_attributes.csv onto network nodes; validate uniqueness and missing values.
From mask-wearing time series, build per-day features: neighbor_mask_share by layer, received_info, prior state.
Identify mandate/enforcement intervals via metadata or structural breaks in adoption curves.
Enable stratified calibration and evaluation (adoption_by_degree_quantile, group inequality).

calibration_strategy.calibration_approach: Use a two-stage procedure: (1) Estimate behavioral parameters with a discrete-time hazard model (logit or complementary log-log) on the panel data: P(wearing_mask_t=1 | wearing_mask_{t-1}, neighbor_mask_share_by_layer, risk_perception, policy, group fixed effects, received_info). This yields initial values for intercepts, coefficients, inertia, and info effect. Include layer-specific neighbor shares to estimate layer_weights and within-group multipliers. (2) Perform simulation-based refinement with Bayesian or simulation optimization (e.g., Approximate Bayesian Computation SMC or Nelder-Mead on a loss function) to match full time-series moments and network-sensitive metrics (overall_adoption_rate_over_time, cascade_size_distribution, norm_churn_rate, adoption_by_degree_quantile). Penalize deviations using weighted sum of squared differences and distributional distances (e.g., Wasserstein for cascades).
calibration_strategy.validation_strategy: Hold out the last 20–30% of days as a temporal test set. Fit on the training period, simulate forward from the last training day state, and compare predicted vs observed curves and metrics on the test set. Additionally, conduct k-fold cross-validation across agent strata (e.g., by occupation) to test generalization. Perform posterior predictive checks for cascade sizes and churn. Use counterfactual toggles (policy on/off) to estimate policy_attribution_fraction; validate attribution by comparing to observed breaks in targeted groups.

file_summaries:
Semantic metadata summary for agent_attributes.csv

- Overall structure and type
  - CSV file; one row per agent (flat, tabular).
  - Columns: agent_id (int), age_group (string/categorical), occupation (string/categorical), risk_perception (float in [0,1]).

- Meaning of columns
  - agent_id: Unique primary key for each agent; use as node ID and to join with network edges or time-series outputs.
  - age_group: Demographic segment (e.g., Youth, Young Adult, Middle Age); can proxy homophily, contact environments, and policy targeting.
  - occupation: Socioeconomic/role category (e.g., Student, Blue Collar, White Collar); implies daily contact context (school vs workplace), degree distribution, and policy relevance.
  - risk_perception: Baseline perceived health risk [0–1]; higher values imply greater intrinsic propensity to adopt mask-wearing and/or lower social threshold for adoption.

- Relationships or nesting
  - No nested elements; fully flat.
  - agent_id is the sole key; age_group and occupation define categorical strata that can be cross-classified (e.g., Youth–Student).
  - Intended to be linked to a separate social network (edges) via agent_id; otherwise supports synthetic network generation with homophily.

- How to inform simulation entities and interactions
  - Agent initialization: Create one Agent per row with attributes {age_group, occupation, risk_perception}.
  - Initial behavior: Set initial mask-wearing probability p0 as a function of risk_perception and group priors (age/occupation-specific baselines).
  - Social influence dynamics:
    - Threshold or logistic adoption models where required social signal decreases as risk_perception increases (e.g., adopt if neighbor signal > 1 − risk_perception).
    - Weight influence/imitability by demographics (e.g., stronger within same age_group/occupation).
  - Network formation/mixing:
    - Use age_group and occupation to impose homophily and context-specific subgraphs (school clusters for Students; workplace clusters for workers; differing degree distributions for Blue vs White Collar).
  - Policy and shocks:
    - Target interventions by occupation (e.g., workplace mandates) or age_group; adjust adoption utility/thresholds accordingly.
  - Validation/constraints:
    - Ensure agent_id uniqueness; risk_perception ∈ [0,1]; categorical values standardized; handle missing values before simulation.

Semantic metadata summary for social_network.json

- Overall structure and type:
  - JSON object (dictionary) where each top-level entry represents an individual (agent) in a multiplex social network.
  - Values are nested objects containing arrays of integers; arrays list connections (adjacency lists) for different relationship layers.

- Meaning of keys:
  - Top-level keys: stringified agent IDs (e.g., "0", "1", …). These represent unique individuals; convert to integers for modeling.
  - Nested keys:
    - family: strong-tie household/kin connections.
    - work_school: workplace or school peers/colleagues.
    - community: broader community/social contacts outside family and work/school.
  - Array values: neighbor agent IDs (integers) indicating ties on that layer.

- Relationships and nested elements:
  - Multiplex network with three layers; an agent can be connected to the same neighbor on multiple layers.
  - Arrays are adjacency lists per layer; edges may or may not be reciprocal (undirectedness is not guaranteed by the data—verify or symmetrize if needed).
  - Some agents may have empty lists for certain layers (sparse or missing ties).
  - ID range in sample suggests roughly 0–99 (likely N≈100), but confirm by scanning all keys and values.

- How this informs simulation entities and interactions:
  - Each agent: create a node with ID plus state variables (e.g., mask_wearing boolean/probability, susceptibility to influence).
  - Edges: construct layer-specific graphs or a single graph with edge attribute layer ∈ {family, work_school, community}.
  - Influence scheduling/weights: differentiate contact frequency/strength by layer (e.g., family > work_school > community) to set:
    - Interaction rates per timestep (e.g., daily family/work, less frequent community).
    - Influence weights in adoption rules (thresholds, weighted contagion, or probabilistic imitation).
  - Initialization: seed initial mask-wearers randomly or by layer; ensure correct casting of string keys to int IDs.
  - Consistency handling: check for asymmetries (add missing reciprocals if modeling undirected ties), remove duplicates, handle self-loops if present.
  - Multiplex effects: allow cumulative influence across layers or layer-specific norms; optionally track cross-layer redundancy (same neighbor on multiple layers increases effective influence).

Semantic metadata summary (for mask-wearing diffusion simulation)

- Data structure and type
  - CSV; each row is a time-stamped observation of an agent’s state.
  - Panel (long) format: multiple records per agent across days.
  - Types: day (int), agent_id (int), wearing_mask (bool), received_info (bool).

- Meaning of columns
  - day: Discrete time step (likely daily, 0-indexed).
  - agent_id: Unique identifier for an agent (node in the social network).
  - wearing_mask: Agent’s behavioral state at that day.
  - received_info: Whether the agent received pro-mask information/exposure that day (from neighbors or exogenous sources).

- Relationships / keys
  - Composite key (day, agent_id) defines a unique state record.
  - Grouping by agent_id over day yields an agent’s trajectory.
  - No nested structures in CSV; temporal linkage is implicit via consecutive days.

- How this informs simulation entities/interactions
  - Agents: Instantiate one agent per unique agent_id with state variables: wearing_mask(t), received_info(t).
  - Time progression: Advance in discrete days; update states per agent each step.
  - Dynamics:
    - Information propagation: received_info(t) indicates exposure; in simulation, this would be driven by social network neighbors and/or global campaigns (network data not present here and must be provided or synthesized).
    - Behavior adoption: wearing_mask(t+1) transitions probabilistically based on wearing_mask(t), received_info(t), and neighbor influence parameters (to be calibrated).
  - Initialization: Use day 0 rows as initial conditions.
  - Calibration/learning: If multiple days exist in the full file, estimate transition probabilities (e.g., P(wearing_mask(t+1)=True | received_info(t), wearing_mask(t))) and validate diffusion curves.
